All four queries are independent and can be issued simultaneously.

decision.decision_reason: Iteration 1 successfully identified the primary CDC NoroSTAT surveillance pages, several high-quality news/clinical media sources with quantified outbreak counts for December 2024 and January 2025, and one state-level source (Minnesota). However, critical gaps remain: (1) No data covering January–February 2025 weekly outbreak counts beyond the week ending Jan. 9 has been surfaced in snippets; (2) The CDC NORS dashboard for structured outbreak-level records (with subnational location, setting, hospitalizations, deaths) was not directly returned as a result; (3) Only one state health department source (Minnesota) appeared — subnational/locality coverage is thin; (4) CDC cruise ship outbreak data for December 2024 was mentioned in a CIDRAP snippet but not directly sourced; (5) Deaths and hospitalizations fields remain unaddressed by any snippet; (6) The February 2025 portion of the time window has no coverage yet. A second iteration targeting: (a) the CDC NORS dashboard directly, (b) February 2025 norovirus data, (c) additional state-level outbreak reports, and (d) CDC cruise ship/vessel outbreak data will materially improve coverage of the target fields.
decision.coverage_assessment: Partial. The Dec 2024 – early Jan 2025 window has good national-level outbreak count coverage via NoroSTAT snippets (495 outbreaks Aug–Dec 11 2024; 91 outbreaks week of Dec 5; 128 outbreaks week prior to Jan 9; 97 outbreaks week ending Jan 9). The Feb 2025 window is entirely uncovered. Subnational/locality coverage is limited to one Minnesota state health department result. Deaths and hospitalizations are not yet evidenced in any snippet. The NORS structured database — the primary source for outbreak-level records with setting, cases, hospitalizations, deaths — was not returned as a direct result despite being queried.
decision.source_diversity_assessment: Moderate. Sources span CDC official pages (5 results), clinical/medical media (contemporarypediatrics.com, mdedge.com, infectiousdiseaseadvisor.com, contagionlive.com), general news (today.com, cbsnews.com, nbcnews.com), academic (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov), and one state health department (health.state.mn.us). Social media (facebook.com, instagram.com, youtube.com) and non-authoritative mirrors (restoredcdc.org) are present but low-value. Missing: direct NORS database results, additional state health department pages, CDC vessel/cruise ship outbreak page, and any WHO/PAHO or ProMED international situation report referencing US norovirus.
decision.trustworthiness_assessment: High for CDC-origin results. The cdc.gov NoroSTAT data page and data table are authoritative. Clinical media (contemporarypediatrics.com, mdedge.com, infectiousdiseaseadvisor.com) cite CDC figures directly and are acceptable collection-support sources. CIDRAP (cidrap.umn.edu) is a highly trusted academic public health news outlet. The Minnesota state health department result is authoritative for subnational data. restoredcdc.org is a mirror/archive site — lower trust, should be deprioritized in favor of the primary cdc.gov URL. Social media results are not usable as evidence sources.
decision.disease_location_time_fit_assessment: Disease fit: Excellent — all accepted results are norovirus-specific. Location fit: Good for national US level; weak for subnational. Time fit: Partial — December 2024 and early January 2025 are covered; mid-January through February 2025 is not yet evidenced in snippets. The task window ends Feb 28, 2025, so the latter half of the window needs targeted follow-up.
decision.corroboration_potential_assessment: Good for national outbreak counts (multiple sources corroborate the 495 Aug–Dec 11 figure and the Jan 9 weekly counts). Weak for subnational, deaths, hospitalizations, and February 2025 data — these fields need additional targeted queries. The PMC article on GII.17 predominance provides virological context but not case/death counts for the target fields.

top_result_summaries.title: Norovirus cases rise ahead of holiday season, CDC data shows
top_result_summaries.snippet: Norovirus cases have risen in the United States in recent weeks, according to data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Nearly 14% of tests for the illness came back positive during the week that ended on Nov. 15, according to CDC data. Over 2,700 tests were conducted that week, according to the CDC, meaning that about 380 cases of norovirus were diagnosed in that period. That's more than double the percentage of positive tests recorded about three months ago, when test positivity in the U.S. this year was at its lowest. The week that ended on Aug. 9 saw a 6.53% positivity rate of more than 4,240 tests conducted during that period, according to CDC data. Norovirus, sometimes known as the stomach bug or stomach flu, is the leading cause of vomiting and diarrhea in the United States, according to the CDC. Millions of people are sickened with norovirus every year, the CDC says, and about 2,500 outbreaks of norovirus are reported in the U.S. each year.

Norovirus cases are surging across the United States this winter, with 91 outbreaks reported by state health departments in the week of Dec. 5 alone, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Each year, about 2,500 norovirus outbreaks are reported in the United States, mostly from November to April. However, this data may not be comprehensive, as health departments are not required to report individual norovirus cases, and doctor’s offices typically don’t test for the virus. A person infected with norovirus usually experiences symptoms within 12 to 48 hours. Norovirus is spread through direct contact with someone who is infected or contaminated surfaces and food. The CDC will continue to monitor norovirus activity.
